To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a multi-class image database of hair detection in the Wild, Figaro, has been created; 2) hair detection can be achieved with high accuracy without relying on a priori human-body part classifiers, and 3) the proposed method is comparable with state-of-the-art approaches on challenging hair detection databases.
we propose a novel hair detection method that is able to detect hair with a very high accuracy (85%) and we propose Figaro, the first multi-class hair detection database.

we present a new multi-class image database called Figaro, which contains images of people in the wild, and we propose a new approach to the problem of hair segmentation in the wild, based on the use of HOG and LTP texture features, and a graph-based multiple segmenter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel methods and tools for the analysis and processing of visual data.
the development and analysis of a novel method for hair segmentation in images, and with the development of a novel image dataset for hair detection.
the following contributions: (1) a novel hair detection dataset, Figaro; (2) a novel multi-class random forest classifier; (3) a new graph-based segmentation method.

the Figaro database is a challenging benchmark for hair segmentation in the wild.
the results are promising and the proposed approach is able to detect hair even when it is partially occluded, but it is still not able to handle the presence of hair on other parts of the body.

the results obtained on Figaro are comparable to the state-of-the-art, but the proposed approach has the advantage of working without relying on a priori information related to the head shape and location.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, by using a random forest based approach, we achieve comparable segmentation accuracy to state-of-the art methods on challenging databases.
we are able to detect hair even in the wild without relying on any a-priori knowledge on head location and shape.
, we have proposed a method for hair detection in wild images, and we have collected a novel multi-class hair database.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the problem of hair segmentation is still challenging, and that a large scale database for hair detection is needed.
, even without any a-priori assumption on head shape, we achieve good performance on hair detection in the real world.
the Figaro database can be used as a benchmark for hair detection in images and videos, as well as to test the effectiveness of different approaches to the task.
